question: Which of the following former Indian test cricketers was NOT known for wicket keeping?
solution:
The correct answer is __**B S Chandrasekhar**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **B. S. Chandrasekhar**:

 
 
• He was a prominent leg-spin bowler and is renowned for his exceptional bowling skills, particularly during the 1970s and 1980s.
 
• He did not play as a wicketkeeper.
 
• He is well-known for his exceptional bowling, which earned him a reputation as one of the greatest spinners in the history of cricket.
 
• He played a key role in many of India’s victories, particularly in Tests against strong teams.
 
• He took over 200 Test wickets and was known for his unique bowling action and ability to spin the ball sharply.

• P. G. Joshi
 
 
• Full Name: Prakash Ganesh Joshi
 
• Role: Wicketkeeper-Batsman
 
• Joshi played for India in the late 1970s and early 1980s. He was known for his skills behind the stumps and also contributed as a lower-order batsman.
 
• He was a part of the Indian squad during a time when wicketkeeping was crucial, especially in Test matches.
 
 
 
• F. M. Engineer
 
 
• Full Name: Farokh Maneksha Engineer
 
• Role: Wicketkeeper-Batsman
 
• Engineer played for India from 1961 to 1975 and is remembered as one of the best wicketkeepers of his time.
 
• He played a significant role in the Indian cricket team and was part of the team that reached the semi-finals of the 1975 Cricket World Cup.
 
• He was known for his agile wicketkeeping skills and his ability to play crucial innings.
 
 
 
• N. S. Tamhane
 
 
• Full Name: Narayan Shripad Tamhane
 
• Role: Wicketkeeper-Batsman
 
• Tamhane was active in the 1950s and is known for his role as a wicketkeeper in the Indian cricket team.
 
• He played in the early days of Indian Test cricket.
 
• While his playing career was shorter than some of his contemporaries, he contributed to the development of wicketkeeping in Indian cricket during his time
